q: Who picks the music for GTA radio stations?
a: Rockstar's in-house music team, led since the GTA IV era by Director of Music Ivan Pavlovich, with Sam Houser as the documented final voice on taste. Outside artists such as Flying Lotus and DJ Pooh have curated or guided whole stations.

q: Why did the first GTA have radio stations?
a: DMA Design musician Craig Conner had written demos in many genres, and audio manager Colin Anderson proposed one station per genre instead of cutting most of them. GTA shipped in 1997 with seven stations of original music.

q: Did Sam Houser work in the music industry?
a: Yes. He started at BMG Records in London in 1990, worked on pop videos and VHS releases, and was head of development at BMG Interactive by 1996.

q: Did the Housers come out of 1990s London raves?
a: Nothing on record says so. Their documented club link is Rockstar Loft, a New York club night Sam Houser and Terry Donovan started in 1999 with Body & Soul's John Davis, which wound down in 2000.

q: How many songs did Rockstar consider for GTA V?
a: The team planned to license over 900 tracks and narrowed them to 241. Ivan Pavlovich gave Rolling Stone a launch figure of 240 licensed songs in 2013.

q: Who composed the GTA VI score?
a: Justice. Their score song "Pusher" came out October 29, 2026, with a 30-track score album due December 11, 2026.
